name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+24 partisan lean in a deep-red East Texas district
Incumbent Moran running with a large fundraising advantage ($1.8M vs $9K)
No competitive polling; prediction markets give Democrats ~2%
Democratic challenger has minimal resources and no outside support
model.rationale: The fundamentals strongly favor Safe R: a heavily Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and a Democratic challenger with negligible fundraising. Markets and the baseline model both point to a roughly 20-point Republican win, so I stay at the baseline.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing the race inside single digits, or a major outside-spending intervention, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-01 is a deeply Republican East Texas district with a partisan lean of about R+24. Incumbent Nathaniel Moran is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination, and he holds a commanding financial edge, having raised roughly $1.8 million with over $770,000 on hand. Democratic nominee Yolanda Prince has raised under $10,000 and has essentially no cash remaining, with no outside spending on either side.

There are no public polls of the general election and no expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which give Democrats only about a 2% chance. The baseline model points to a Republican margin near 20 points, and nothing in the evidence justifies moving away from it. This race is rated Safe R with high confidence.
